body: Thanks for the info, I was also the one who opened that Firefox bug. My personal preference here would be for both `:hover` and `:active` to apply to the `` and the `` when interacting with the area. That seems the most useful and intuitive to me and doesn't remove any functionality from any engine. Also, ``s aren't entirely invisible. In all browsers, an `` is focusable via tabbing through the document if it has an `href` attribute. In that case, every browser draws a correctly-shaped outline (rectangle/circle/polygon) on the image where you'd expect it. This can easily be seen in the [examples on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/area) or when adding an `href` to the dog testcase. Also, in Chrome, it additionally renders as a regular empty inline element wherever it is in the DOM, though this seems very undesirable. (Can be seen in the bottom right corner of the image when adding `outline: 25px solid red;` to the `#head:active` selector in the dog testcase and clicking on the dogs head)

> From what I can tell, the spec doesn't define any of this. It's defined in https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#pseudo-classes > When you click a region defined by an `` (over the top of an ``), Firefox and Safari consider the `img` element to be `:active`, whereas Chrome considers the `` to be `:active`. Then it seems Chrome matches the spec. Options: 1. Leave the spec as-is; change for Gecko and WebKit. 2. Make the `img` match `:active` instead; change for Chromium. 3. Make the `img` also match `:active` when an `area` matches `:active` (like `label` makes its control also match `:active`); change for everyone.
